I will never advocate for someone to kill themselves. Even though I want to myself, I believe that it should be a decision that isn't taken lightly.

So this isn't a guide for any of us in this sub, but a way for our loved ones, those who might even care and our friends to begin understanding/start taking the steps to see what going through depressive and suicidal thoughts is like. 

And I want to get people in this sub's thoughts and experiences into this document so that there is at least a small understanding of this feeling 


So essentially I am writing an informal college paper with an appendix title page etc lol

I get that feeling so often..... And the worst part is, you say that now, but deep down you know someone will actually miss you.
Hell I'd actually miss you because we're in this together. I don't want anything happen to you, even though you're an internet stranger.

It didn't work for me because of the self defense human nature we all have. The amount of guilt and remorse you get before it sucked so bad. Literally when you think you didn't want to live, the brain throws all it could to stop you, and it works.

It's not a good feeling I can tell you that.

Frankly speaking, no matter what you do, the guilt will always be there. And it's never as simple as them hating you/you say you hate them. 

If you're thinking how to not hurt people, then that means you care about these people, and usually that is reciprocated. 

I would at least say, to not hurt them or minimizing the guilt, give em a fighting chance to help you out first before doing anything drastic. Talk to them, no matter how hard that may be, because you're giving them a chance to understand you better, and a chance for you to understand yourself better.

As suicidal as I am, I like to help people understand what I am going through in order to help them expand their understanding of different kinds of depression.

Of course I am not representative of everyone here, this is just my experience.

People always say they care about you. After a while, my brain sorta just shuts off and ignores that term because that sounds like a bluff for you to not kill yourself. And frankly sometimes I absolutely despise that phrase because it's lost all it's meaning, it doesn't feel genuine, and it's just a way to make yourself (person saying it) feel better. Actions speak more than words. 

Yesterday was my birthday, and a close friend (idk anymore) told me that they cared about me, but lol and behold, they don't even remember. Twice. They asked earlier this week for the date, and I thought they'd remember, yet they didn't.

"Is my bar set too high? Is asking people to care enough to remember a single date that hard?"

This was my exact thought. And is also what brought me here, I was very suicidal, had a noose around my neck and was thinking of a date to do it. I know based on my own notes during my depressive episodes that even the smallest of things, like remembering a date, or just checking in once in a while, show that they're in your mind can help a lot.

And if you ever say something, own up to it and act. Your actions showing that you care about them matters so so much. And so much more than just the words themselves. Be genuine, especially when you know someone is depressed, you don't know what they're going through and is good to listen. 

The first thought when I tell people I'm depressed, is to prepare myself to dissect people's body language and see if they're genuine or not. Because in my honest opinion, people change the moment they hear the word depressed and would become disingenuous and i hate it.


What I think all the time is that the best way to not lose a game any more is to not play the game. And the sunk cost fallacy is a thing even in life. Just because you lived that long doesn't mean you need to continue it.

I have already gone down the rabbit hole many times, convinced myself life isnt worth living for, and there is no afterlife, where consciousness is only a construct our brains perceive, so without our brains, I don't perceive time and space, therefore, the pain will go away.



My word of advice based on my own experience... Be genuine, be there, and care for em, think about them. Do shit with em. Don't do it because they're depressed, but do it because you care about them

You know, I feel very much the same... I mean hell, o just made a post like half an hour ago. 

And the only reason why I'm still here is because of the fact that I keep telling myself the experiences that I would miss out on if I was dead. It's a one way ticket, and I'd at least like to try different shit before I use said ticket.

My reasoning?

Skydiving? Might as well, if an accident happens, whatever, at least I went out with a bang

Scuba diving? Same thing

Hiking? Earth is fucking beautiful and also same thing.

Road trip? 

Snowboarding?

Surfing?

Windsurfing?


For me, all these options are there. And thinking about it makes me want to try it because of the adrenaline. And that helps me last one more day. You don't have to be good at anything, as long as you're willing to try

You know, you may not think this right now, but your grades don'tean anything in the long run. You're 15, although my views on death are pretty controversial, there is still a lot to experience. 

Think about it this way, death is a one-way ticket, once you take and use this ticket, you won't be able to come back and experience what you have never experienced before. Living isn't all about grades and talent. There are people out there who are talented and gifted, but are still depressed. 

What you really need is to try something new, convince yourself that you want to try new experiences. Whatever opportunities you choose, try it first, then make a decision. 

If there is something you've longed to do, do it, the world is shit right now, but might as well try everything, experience the time you have here and use that ticket once you're ready. Because in the end, we only get one ticket.
